```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library("naboer")
```

The fold object keeps canonical data and compressed indices. Contiguous temporal
memberships use shared ordering and range endpoints; repeated spatial/taxon sets
share membership definitions. Fixed-station space-time queries search temporal
intervals for neighbouring station geometries. Analysis sets are complements and
are not stored as duplicated vectors.

```{r}
x <- tibble::tibble(time = seq_len(1000))
folds <- neighbourhoods(x,
  index = time,
  temporal = temporal_window(time_span(3, "seconds"))
)
print(folds)
tibble::as_tibble(folds, folds = c(1, 500, 1000))
diagnostics <- summary(folds)
diagnostics[c("assessment_size", "omission_size", "omitted_fraction", "unassessed")]
```

`as_tibble()` omits membership list-columns unless `membership = TRUE`.
`assessment_indices()`, `omission_indices()` and `analysis_indices()` expand only
requested folds; asking for all folds is explicit but can consume large amounts
of memory. `summary()` reports assessment coverage without retaining expanded
memberships. Plot selected folds with `ggplot2::autoplot(folds, folds = 1)`.

## Materialising nei

`mgcv` consumes packed observation indices. This output is proportional to the
total membership count even when the fold object is compact. Export checks the
integer-index limit and estimates output bytes before allocation. The default
1 GiB guard can be adjusted explicitly:

```{r}
nei <- as_nei(folds, max_bytes = 100 * 1024^2)
sum(vapply(nei, length, integer(1)))
```

The estimate covers packed integer arrays, not the total R process or temporary
allocation peaks. Use a limit below available memory. Sampling bam neighbourhood
criteria does not remove the requirement to define all neighbourhoods. Forecast
designs retain compressed future exclusions until export, which can itself be
quadratic in the number of observations/origins.

`as_rset()` materialises analysis complements as well as assessment membership.
For a million-row LOO design, these analysis vectors alone need about 4 TB,
despite the compact native representation. Conversion has its own `max_bytes`
guard using the same 1 GiB default. This estimate covers index vectors, not the
additional list, split and data overhead in rsample. Convert only feasible
designs and use a memory budget below available process memory.

Output size is separate from model-fitting cost. In particular, discrete
`bam()` NCV needs neighbourhood-sized matrix inversions and can be impractical
for large blocks even if the exported integer arrays fit in memory. See
[mgcv's bam documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/mgcv/html/bam.html).

## Reproducible benchmarks

The source repository's `benchmarks/` directory contains R scripts for million-row
multiple-series data, fixed monitoring stations, moving locations, polygons and
approximation studies. They are excluded from routine CRAN tests. Records should
include input dimensions, memberships, compressed/output sizes, runtime,
R heap high-water or process peak memory (clearly distinguished), hardware,
R/dependency versions and brute-force agreement on sampled focal observations.

Dense windows are deliberately tested with preallocation guards. A sparse
million-row design and a dense million-row design have very different output
costs; construction runtime does not predict packed size.
